## HeuristicTablePluginConfig.growBeyondHeight property

When true, an explicit `height` on the table, or on any of its cells, is treated as a minimum: the box still grows to fit content taller than it. When false, that `height` is enforced as written and taller content overflows it.

**Signature:**

```typescript
growBeyondHeight?: boolean;
```

## Remarks

Per [CSS 2.1 §17.5.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/tables.html#height-layout)<!-- -->, `height` on a `table`<!-- -->, `tr`<!-- -->, `th` or `td` box is only a minimum, so `true` is the faithful reading of the HTML. It is off by default because React Native has no table layout algorithm to shrink a row back down, and a document whose markup sizes its tables is better served by a box that stays the size it asked for.
